resources.string: Enable to control editing from notification
Like God, remove any elements on the interface that you don\'t like
Show or hide app icon from launcher

1. Overview
GodMode is an Xposed module that can block unwanted elements (buttons, ads, text, etc.) on any app\'s interface.

2. Enable/Disable
1. Master Switch: Settings → General → GodMode switch.
  - When enabled, a notification appears showing "Start editor".
  - When disabled, edit mode is forced off and the notification disappears.
2. Notification Toggle: With master switch on, tap the notification to toggle between "Start editor" and "Exit editor".

3. Edit Mode Operations
When edit mode is active, a toolbar appears on the right side of the target app:

1. Tap to Select: Tap any element on the screen to select it (red overlay follows).
2. Long Press to Block: Long press an element (~0.5s), it turns green.
  - Drag the green overlay to the top green area and release → cancel.
  - Release elsewhere → particle animation plays, element disappears, rule saved.
3. Volume Keys: Press and release volume up/down to show/hide the toolbar. When toolbar is visible, volume keys navigate between elements.
4. SeekBar Slider: Drag the slider to select elements at different hierarchy levels.
5. ⬆⬇ Buttons: Manually switch to previous/next element.
6. 🔀 Button: Toggle toolbar position (right/left).
7. 👁 Button: Preview block effect — temporarily hides the selected element, tap again to restore.
8. 🚫 Button: Block the currently selected element (same as long press).

4. Rule Management
- View rules: Settings → App Rules → tap package name.
- View details: Rule list → tap entry, swipe left/right.
- Delete single rule: Rule details → menu → Delete rule.
- Delete all rules: Rule list → menu → Delete rules.
- Backup rules: Rule list/details → menu → Backup rules.
- Restore rules: Settings → menu → Restore rules.

5. Notes
- Edit mode only works in third-party apps where the module is activated in Xposed/LSPosed.
- Launcher, system UI, input methods, UI-less apps, and GodMode itself are not editable.
- If a crash occurs, a dialog will appear on next launch to copy the crash log.
Notification permission denied, notification switch will not be shown
You can try using GodMode to block annoying buttons. If you encounter issues, don\'t worry, they will be fixed soon!
